title: Topic 2.1: The Bible as a Guide

pages.lesson:
LESSON: THE BIBLE AS A GUIDE

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Bible
Topic 2.1: The Bible as a Guide

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on The Bible as a Guide. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should the Bible guide us in daily life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the benefits of reading the Bible
2. read the Bible always to grow spiritually

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: THE BIBLE AS A GUIDE
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
The Bible as a Guide helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: THE BIBLE AS A GUIDE
Study The Bible as a Guide like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the benefits of reading the Bible

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the benefits of reading the Bible. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the benefits of reading the Bible.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “The Bible as a Guide” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the benefits of reading the Bible. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read the Bible always to grow spiritually

What this means
In this part you learn to read the Bible always to grow spiritually. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read the Bible always to grow spiritually.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Bible as a Guide in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read the Bible always to grow spiritually. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what The Bible as a Guide is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “The Bible as a Guide” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify the benefits of reading the Bible)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Bible as a Guide in your own words. (skill: read the Bible always to grow spiritually)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach The Bible as a Guide to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the benefits of reading the Bible.
3. Practise this skill: read the Bible always to grow spiritually.
4. Make one local Kenya example of The Bible as a Guide from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for The Bible as a Guide: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study The Bible as a Guide?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should the Bible guide us in daily life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what The Bible as a Guide means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the benefits of reading the Bible.
5. Be able to: read the Bible always to grow spiritually.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
